finding_authoritative_dap_spec_section_6.content_verbatim:
6   Failure Posture
DAP-28   Every gate in DAP fails closed. An approval service that cannot be reached, a metering write that cannot complete, a terms resolution that returns nothing, a ceiling check that errors — each refuses the operation. No path returns estate data, an artefact, or a query result when a governing check could not complete. [FPT_FLS.1]
DAP-29   A metered event that cannot be written to the Ledger refuses the operation it meters. An unrecorded extraction is not permitted to have happened. [I-4 pattern]
DAP-30   Browse degrades rather than refuses: where the census is stale or partially unavailable, DAP returns what it has, marked as stale with its as-of time, and never silently presents an incomplete estate as complete. [honesty grammar]

q7_disposition_supported_by_finding.authoritative_source_says: DAP-Spec §6 (Failure Posture · DAP-28/29/30) speaks ONLY of gates failing closed (approval, metering write, terms resolution, ceiling check, [journey adds redaction pass and release budget]). It does NOT define a separate non-gate execution fault state, and it does NOT define a fourth kind of Blocked.
q7_disposition_supported_by_finding.journey_open_question_line_247_verbatim: Does a non-gate execution fault exist as its own state? DAP-28 covers gates failing closed; it says nothing about a fault with no gate involved — a training job crashing mid-run for a reason unrelated to approval, redaction, metering, or the budget. If that's a real case, it may need a state Blocked doesn't cover, or Blocked needs a fourth kind. Unconfirmed either way.
